services.name: In-home therapy session (2 hours)
services.story: A public program family: nothing is taken; the practice bills the program its own way, and the family pays nothing.

services_shape: clinic: a child with autism gets many sessions a week (often 10 to 40 hours) on a set weekly schedule, at the center, at home, or at school or daycare with the school's OK; each session is one-to-one with a behavior technician from the child's small team, under a supervising analyst; the analyst joins some sessions to supervise and meets the parents for training; the health plan's approval sets the hours for about 6 months at a time
questions_before_times: has the child been diagnosed (most plans need the diagnosis report)
where therapy would happen: at the center, at home, or at school or daycare
how many hours a week the family hopes for, and which days and times work
a health plan, self-pay or a public program (only the name here)
safety_stop: a child is missing (ran off from the center or a home session), a seizure over 5 minutes, trouble breathing, or a serious injury
suicide or self-harm words from a parent, a teen, or the child
first_steps: Diagnosis report and the doctor's referral
Treatment plan signed by the parent
license: the practice's own word, optional: each behavior analyst's national certification and any state license the practice names; each behavior technician's own registration; the practice's own license if it has one. Rosie never looks a license up and never says one is checked
staff_skills: behavior analyst, behavior technician, trained on a given child's plan (per child), parent training, social skills groups, home sessions, school sessions, toddlers, Spanish, sign language
messages_never: the child's diagnosis, behaviors, health, session data, progress and plan details never go in a text: only the secure page; texts say only the practice's name, the day, the time and the place, and name the child only by first initial
demo_note: Demo data for testing only. [G] = prefilled from the business's Google listing at sign-up; the owner checks each field.
